text:
violet: quick brain dump 1: we're running into ENI / public IP quotas with per-tenant private endpoints + ephemeral egress IPs. two proposals: (A) allocate per-tenant elastic IPs and announce via BGP (transit-gw/edge-router) or (B) keep small shared pool and API-route advertise per-tenant via route table updates. tradeoffs?

henry: BGP wins on convergence + no API rate limits. announcement is instant on the network plane (mostly). but requires control of BGP session and edge router state per-tenant -> state explosion. also harder for on-prem/private installs.

kai: API-route (RT updates / ENI attach/detach) is simpler operationally and cloud-native. downside: slow (~30-90s) route propagation, and we hit API rate limits at scale. also transient blackholes when ENI moves.

violet: major constraints: 1) some customers need stable egress IP for whitelists 2) we want autoscaling (IPs churn) 3) minimize operator overhead for dedicated/private installs.

henry: suggestion: hybrid model. for high-SLA tenants use EIP + BGP announced prefixes (reserved, sticky). for bulk low-SLA tenants use shared-pool + API routing with connection-proxy fallback. split by account tier.

kai: operational detail: BGP requires us to advertise per-tenant /32s? that will flood peers unless we aggregate. we can do per-tenant /32s but must ask backbone/peers for support; otherwise use a pool per-region and do NAT mapping internally.

violet: question: what about ephemeral reclaim policy? when a tenant scales down we want to reclaim IPs quickly, but if partner whitelists are still pointing to that IP we break them. any heuristics?

henry: hold IP in a 'grace' state for TTL_window = max(whitelist_ttl, 3600s). default 1h. have an opt-out APi so customers can request sticky EIP (no reclaim).

kai: another idea: soft-announce + proto-priority degrade. sequence: 1) when moving IP -> announce new mapping via API (or BGP) 2) after 10s start mapping with higher preference 3) keep old mapping pinned for 60m but with lower route priority so that peers still accept it for whitelisted partners to transition. needs route priority support on transit.

violet: operational scripts snippet for reclaim daemon (pseudo-bash):

```bash
# reclaim loop
for ip in $(./list-ephemeral-ips --idle); do
  mark_grace $ip --until "$(date -d '+1 hour' +%s)"
  notify-customer $ip "Your ephemeral IP $ip will be reclaimed in 1h unless you request sticky EIP"
done
# GC job later: reclaim if grace expired and no sticky flag
```

henry: metrics we need: ephemeral_ip_reclaim_rate, ephemeral_ip_grace_count, eip_sticky_requests, route_update_latency_seconds. Alerts: reclaim_rate > baseline or route_update_latency p95>30s.

kai: cloud quotas note: ENI attach rate can be burst-limited. when scaling up many endpoints at once, we should stagger attach by sharding key. sample terraform-ish plan: create placeholder ENIs in advance up to buffer N, attach on demand.

violet: does per-tenant BGP make compliance harder for Private deployments? some customers don't want us to peer into their VPCs.

henry: yes for private/on-prem customers we should prefer API-route or provide an option for customer-managed BGP (we provide config + certs and they run BGP sessions on their edge). avoid unilateral peering into customer-managed networks.

oncall: ops automation ask: add a paged runbook for IP reclaim incidents with steps: identify impacted tenants, check whitelist requests, apply sticky flag, and re-run announce. link template: https://our.internal/runbooks/ip-reclaim. also add a postmortem checklist for broken webhooks.

violet: short list of decision items for RFC:
- hybrid model: BGP for Premium, API-route for Standard
- default grace window 1h with opt-out sticky EIP
- pre-warmed ENI buffer per region to avoid attach bursts
- route priority downgrade for 60m on migration
- customer-managed BGP for private installs
- dashboards & alerts (henry list)

henry: +1. add a security check: ensure RPKI/route filtering on our transit so we don't accidentally leak prefixes.

kai: +1. i'll prototype the pre-warm ENI buffer and attach-stagger controller. will post canary results next week.

infra-bot: created issue INFRA-3321: "ephemeral-ip-reclaim-and-route-model" assigned to kai, henry, violet. link: https://our.internal/issues/INFRA-3321

violet: thanks all. i'll draft RFC with the hybrid recommendation and include the scripts and metrics. :rocket:
